context_map.exchanged_information: Async event TurnCompleted (session id, user message, assistant reply) so memory can maintain the rolling summary; Memory's needs (what it must receive to summarize) are negotiated with Orchestration.
context_map.boundary_protection: Only the TurnCompleted event crosses; session ownership checks and turn state stay internal to Orchestration.

context_map.exchanged_information: Synchronous query: current Context Window (last 12 messages + rolling summary, <=16,000 tokens), called by Orchestration at the start of each turn. Memory supplies, Orchestration initiates.
context_map.boundary_protection: Orchestration receives a read-only Context Window view; summarization internals and token accounting stay in Memory.

context_map.exchanged_information: Async events TurnCompleted and ToolCalled (user message, tool call, assistant reply, token counts) appended to the log.
context_map.boundary_protection: History adopts Orchestration's event model as-is and only appends; it never mutates or reaches into turn state.

context_map.exchanged_information: Synchronous query: reload of past chats, called by Orchestration after it has verified session ownership (403 otherwise).
context_map.boundary_protection: Read-only history entries; access control is enforced by Orchestration, History never decides ownership.

context_map.exchanged_information: LLM provider completions/token streams and Spring AI backend tool results, requested by Orchestration during a turn (command/query initiated by Orchestration; supplier stays upstream).
context_map.boundary_protection: Orchestration translates provider and tool models into Turn/Tool Call/Token Stream on its side; 5-call cap and 30s timeout applied here; no provider types leak.

context_map.exchanged_information: LLM provider summarization answer, requested by Memory when folding older messages into the rolling summary.
context_map.boundary_protection: Memory translates the provider response into its Rolling summary; provider model never leaks.

cross_boundary_flows.business_process: Turn completion fans out to memory update
cross_boundary_flows.notes: Mechanism: async event TurnCompleted. WIRED: Memory's consumes list names TurnCompleted and its invariant 'last 12 messages in full detail and older messages only as a running summary'. Failure posture: at-least-once delivery with idempotent summary update keyed by session+turn; retry on LLM failure.

Mechanism: query (Orchestration 'reads' Conversation Memory). Read-after-event: Memory refreshes asynchronously from TurnCompleted, so a quick next message can see a stale window. Staleness posture: serialize - Orchestration does not start the next turn of the same session until Memory has applied the previous TurnCompleted (the last 12 messages are always fresh; only summary freshness is at stake). Memory failure to refresh must not block beyond the 30s turn timeout.

cross_boundary_flows.business_process: Append turn and tool activity to history
cross_boundary_flows.notes: Mechanism: async events TurnCompleted and ToolCalled. WIRED: History consumes both and 'History entries are append-only and each carries token counts'; Orchestration's out_of_scope states 'Persisting history (Chat History Log)'. Ambiguity carried from discovery: delivery posture and dedup identity are unspecified, so a retried message could be logged twice - planning-blocking decision for the history writer: client-supplied idempotency key vs natural identity (turn id + entry sequence; payload excluded since mutable).

Mechanism: query (Orchestration 'reads' Chat History Log). Initiated by Orchestration after ownership check. Slight lag after recent append is acceptable (bounded lag: a just-finished turn may be missing for a moment; cost is a briefly incomplete reload).
Mechanism: synchronous queries to LLM provider and backend tools, non-blocking (no Netty event-loop blocking); results streamed to the user as Token Stream (SSE). Limits: 5 tool calls, 30s.
Mechanism: query (Memory 'reads' LLM provider summarization), executed inside the TurnCompleted handler.
